A simulated range test of the Stoney Lake range model

Source: R/data.R
stoney_range_test.Rd

Hourly counts from a range test on two lines, one in 1 m of water and one in 25 m, the depths that bracket the receivers of stoney_track. Each line held three receivers and five range-test tags, so its 15 pairs span 100 to 1,600 m, for 48 hours: the shallow line from 20 May 2024 and the deep line from 23 May. The detections were simulated with the Stoney example's range model of stoney_track, with no variation between receivers or hours, so a logistic curve fitted at each depth reproduces the example's curve at that depth. The detections, the receivers and the tags of the test are included as files (stoney_range_test_detections.csv, stoney_range_test_receivers.csv and stoney_range_test_tags.csv in system.file("extdata", package = "detfield")), and stoney_range_test is what range_test_counts() makes of them.

Usage

stoney_range_test

Format

A data frame with one row per receiver, tag and hour, 1,440 rows:

datetime

Start of the hour, POSIXct in UTC.

receiver_serial, station_id

The receiver and its station.

depth_m

Depth of the receiver, 1 or 25 m.

transmitter, tag_model

The range-test tag and its model.

distance_m

Distance from the receiver to the tag, in metres.

sent

Transmissions the tag sent in the hour.

heard

Detections of the tag the receiver logged in the hour.

Source

Simulated by https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/detfield/blob/main/data-raw/stoney_range_test.R, which is in the repository and not in the installed package.

See also

stoney_range_covariates for a range test with tag models, wind and variation between receivers and hours.

Examples

aggregate(cbind(heard, sent) ~ depth_m + distance_m, data = stoney_range_test,
          FUN = sum)
